chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:
Acts of kindness protect against evil encounters.

key_terms.صَنَائِعُ الْمَعْرُوفِ: Plural of acts of kindness/benevolence; refers to various good deeds
key_terms.مَصَارِعَ السُّوءِ: Evil encounters/death by misfortune; plural of masra' (place of falling/death)

ai.seo_question: How does performing acts of kindness protect against misfortune according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing a key principle in Shia ethics where diverse acts of benevolence (sanā'i' al-ma'rūf) function as a spiritual shield against unforeseen calamities (masāri' al-sū'). This teaching underscores the metaphysical efficacy of charity and kindness, suggesting that consistent good deeds can divert divine decrees of hardship, a concept deeply rooted in the broader Islamic tradition of 'dafa' (repulsion) through righteous action.
